Centered Log-Ratio Transformation

transform_clr.Rd

This function implements a glycoWork-compatible CLR preprocessing strategy. Data are transformed on the log2 scale following glycowork::clr_transformation(). The log-ratio coordinates are returned directly, with the experiment's scale metadata set to "logx".

Usage

transform_clr(x, by = NULL, gamma = 0.1, group_scales = NULL, seed = 123)

Arguments

x

A glyexp::GlycomicSE(), glyexp::GlycoproteomicSE(), or SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment() object.

by

Either a column name in sample_info or a factor/vector with one value per sample.

gamma

Standard deviation of the scale-uncertainty model on the log2 scale. Default is 0.1. Set to 0 for deterministic transformation.

group_scales

Optional informed group scales. For binary comparisons, this can be a single positive ratio for the second group relative to the first, or two positive scales from which that ratio is derived. For multi-group data, provide a positive vector with one scale per group. All scales and any derived two-group ratio must be finite and strictly positive.

seed

Non-negative integer seed for random number generation. Default is 123. The caller's random state is restored, including on errors.

Value

A container of the same class as x, with a transformed expression matrix. The returned values are log2-ratio coordinates, with scale = "logx" in metadata. Other metadata are preserved, apart from pipeline recording.

Algorithmic details

The stochastic branch follows glycowork: when gamma > 0, CLR noise is sampled per feature-sample entry rather than once per sample. Without informed scales, this corresponds to jittering around the sample-specific log2 geometric mean of the components. The result remains on the log-ratio scale, without exponentiation.

The group_scales argument is interpreted in the same way as glycowork's custom_scale. For exactly two groups, provide the total-signal ratio of the second group relative to the first, either directly as a scalar or implicitly through two per-group scales. For multi-group data, provide one positive scale per group; these scales are used only in the stochastic branch.

Input requirements

CoDA accepts raw, log, log2, and log10 inputs, and rejects logx. On raw input, abundances must be finite and strictly positive. On ordinary log input, finite zero and negative coordinates are valid; -Inf represents zero abundance and is rejected. Missing values and other non-finite values are rejected on all input scales; no pseudo-count or automatic imputation is applied. If zero abundances represent missing observations, first call zero_to_na(), then use an appropriate imputation function to obtain positive values. Choose the imputation method for your data; impute_zero() is not suitable before CoDA. Entirely missing features or samples may need filtering rather than imputation.

Glycoproteomics

For GlycoproteomicSE objects and legacy glycoproteomics experiments, each unique combination of protein and protein_site is treated as a separate composition. CLR centering is performed independently within each site. ALR is not supported for glycoproteomics; use transform_clr() or auto_coda(), which always uses CLR. Both site identifiers must be present and non-missing. by continues to specify sample groups.

The output preserves all rows, their original order, and their annotations.

With gamma = 0 and no informed scales, a site containing a single positive feature returns zero on the log-ratio scale.

Motif quantification

If you intend to use ALR/CLR transformation with motif quantification, you should apply the transformation after motif quantification rather than before. In another words, the recommended workflow is:

  1. Perform data preprocessing.

clean_exp <- auto_clean(exp)

  1. Perform motif quantification on the cleaned experiment.

motif_exp <- glydet::quantify_motifs(clean_exp, motifs)

  1. Perform ALR/CLR transformation on the motif-quantified experiment.

coda_motif_exp <- auto_coda(motif_exp, by = "group", gamma = 0.1)

  1. Proceed with downstream analyses on the transformed motif experiment.

dea_res <- glystats::gly_ttest(coda_motif_exp)

See also

data_scales for working domains and supported input scales.

Examples

x <- glyexp::as_glycoproteomic_se(glyexp::real_experiment)
x <- impute_half_sample_min(zero_to_na(x[seq_len(6), ]))
result <- transform_clr(x, gamma = 0)
get_pipeline(result)
#> 
#> ── <glyclean_pipeline> 3 steps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 1. zero_to_na
#>    (no parameters)
#> 2. impute_half_sample_min
#>    (no parameters)
#> 3. transform_clr
#>    by = NULL, gamma = 0, group_scales = NULL, seed = 123
